reference: GNU gzip invoked from a stock system Bash in the harness reference mode. Fixed RFC 1952 members embedded in fixtures were generated independently with Python's standard-library gzip encoder at mtime=0; compression bytes produced by gzip are not compared because the documented contract allows different compressor choices.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata contracts
stdin/stdout round trips for binary bytes at compression levels 1, 6, and 9 with -n
decoding and integrity testing of independently generated concatenated gzip members
named-file compression/decompression lifecycle, permissions, -k, custom -S suffix, and -f overwrite behavior
CRC corruption, truncation, unknown suffix, hard-link, and symbolic-link handling
Unforced named symlink errors have status 1 even with -q; quiet hard-link warnings retain status 2.
Explicit force follows source symlinks, preserves referent data, and removes only the symlink name unless -k is used.
Stdout/test filters follow ordinary symlinks, and mixed warning/error operands continue with failure precedence.
exclusions: Compression byte identity is intentionally not asserted; the documented interface permits different valid compressed streams.
Recursive traversal, listing statistics, -N name restoration, legacy compress input, and trailing non-gzip data are outside the documented supported interface.
The runner compares file bytes, modes, links, and targets, but not file timestamps.
Link fixtures use stable, ordinary private relative files. Concurrent link/referent changes, unusual destination aliasing, permission changes and filesystem failures are not qualified.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves gzip as a builtin, which is the independent Bash type contract for this loadable.
Confirm help exposes the documented gzip synopsis and core behavior text from the registered builtin metadata.
cases.script: help_text=$(help gzip) || exit 2; [[ $help_text == *'Compress/decompress gzip files or stdin, including concatenated members.'* ]] || exit 3; [[ $help_text == *'-c stdout, -d decompress'* ]] || exit 4; printf 'gzip help metadata present\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise filter mode, -n, clustered-compatible level selection, and binary input/output through GNU gzip and the candidate.
cases.script: for level in 1 6 9; do printf 'bytes:\000\377tail\n' | gzip -n "-$level" -c | gzip -d -c; done

cases.purpose: Decode and test two independently encoded gzip members concatenated in one named file, including a NUL byte in the second member.
Check default named-file compression removes its input, -t accepts the resulting stream, decompression restores the file, and mode bits survive the lifecycle.
cases.script: mkdir area; printf 'permission payload\n' > area/plain; chmod 640 area/plain; gzip area/plain; [[ -f area/plain.gz && ! -e area/plain ]] || exit 21; gzip -t area/plain.gz; gzip -d area/plain.gz; [[ -f area/plain && ! -e area/plain.gz ]] || exit 22; printf 'lifecycle=%s\n' "$(<area/plain)"

cases.purpose: Exercise -k and -S during named-file compression, then use -d with the custom suffix to restore the original path and payload.
cases.script: mkdir area; printf 'custom suffix payload\n' > area/item; chmod 604 area/item; gzip -k -S .packed area/item; [[ -f area/item && -f area/item.packed ]] || exit 31; rm area/item; gzip -d -S .packed area/item.packed; [[ -f area/item && ! -e area/item.packed ]] || exit 32; printf 'custom=%s\n' "$(<area/item)"

cases.purpose: Verify an existing compressed destination is preserved without -f, compare that command's status, then force replacement and decode the fresh payload while keeping the source.
cases.script:
mkdir area; printf 'fresh payload
' > area/input; printf 'stale archive
' > area/input.gz; if gzip -k area/input; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; printf 'no-clobber-status=%s
' "$rc"; [[ $rc -ne 0 && $(<area/input.gz) == 'stale archive' ]] || exit 41; gzip -fk area/input; [[ -f area/input ]] || exit 42; gzip -dc area/input.gz; rm area/input.gz

cases.purpose: Check -t rejects an independently generated member with a deliberately altered CRC trailer and leaves the named input intact; report the gzip command status in stdout for parity comparison.
Check named decompression of an independently encoded but truncated member fails, reports its command status, retains the archive, and does not publish a partial output.
Check -d on a non-gzip-suffixed filename reports a nonzero GNU-compatible status and leaves the input unchanged.
cases.script: printf 'plain input\n' > sample.txt; if gzip -d sample.txt; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; printf 'suffix-status=%s\n' "$rc"; [[ $rc -ne 0 && -f sample.txt && ! -e sample ]]

cases.purpose: Use relative fixture links to confirm gzip refuses a multiply linked regular input and a symbolic-link input without creating compressed outputs or changing link relationships.
cases.script:
printf 'hard linked data
' > hard; ln hard hard.peer; if gzip hard; then hard_rc=0; else hard_rc=$?; fi; printf 'symbolic target
' > target; ln -s target shortcut; if gzip shortcut; then sym_rc=0; else sym_rc=$?; fi; printf 'hard-status=%s symbolic-status=%s
' "$hard_rc" "$sym_rc"; [[ $hard_rc -ne 0 && $sym_rc -ne 0 && -f hard && -f hard.peer && -L shortcut && ! -e hard.gz && ! -e shortcut.gz ]]

cases.purpose: Under -q, ordinary symlink open errors remain status 1 before hard-link/directory classification. Hard-link-only warnings remain quiet with status 2; input links and bytes remain intact.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > target; ln target peer; ln -s target shortcut
mkdir folder; ln -s folder dirlink
for path in shortcut dirlink; do
 rc=0; gzip -q "$path" || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
 printf '%s-status=%s\n' "$path" "$rc"
done
rc=0; gzip -q target 2> quiet-diagnostic || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 && ! -s quiet-diagnostic && target -ef peer && -L shortcut && -L dirlink ]]
printf 'hard-status=%s\n' "$rc"
rm quiet-diagnostic

cases.purpose: GNU -fk follows a private input symlink and keeps both link and referent. Decode the resulting archive before removing only that varying encoded artifact; compare payload, paths and modes.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > target; ln -s target shortcut
gzip -fk shortcut
[[ -L shortcut && -f target && -f shortcut.gz ]]
gzip -dc shortcut.gz > decoded
rm shortcut.gz

cases.purpose: GNU -f follows the source symlink, removes only that input link name, and keeps the referent. Decode and compare all payload/path effects independently of compression byte identity.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > target; ln -s target shortcut
gzip -f shortcut
[[ ! -e shortcut && ! -L shortcut && -f target && -f shortcut.gz ]]
gzip -dc shortcut.gz > decoded
rm shortcut.gz

cases.purpose: Forced named decompression follows an independently encoded archive symlink, removes that link name, preserves the referent archive, and publishes the expected decoded path and bytes.
Stdout compression and integrity-test filters follow private symlinks without removing either link or referent; compare visible payload and all fixture bytes/links.
cases.script:
printf 'payload\n' > target; ln -s target shortcut
gzip -c shortcut | gzip -dc
printf '%b' '\037\213\010\000\000\000\000\000\002\377\313\115\315\115\112\055\322\315\317\113\345\002\000\154\067\215\207\013\000\000\000' > target.gz
ln -s target.gz archive-link.gz
gzip -t archive-link.gz
[[ -L shortcut && -L archive-link.gz && -f target && -f target.gz ]]

cases.purpose: A hard-link warning followed by a symlink error retains status 1 while a later valid file is compressed. Restore that final file and compare all earlier links and data unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'hard\n' > hard; ln hard peer
printf 'target\n' > target; ln -s target shortcut
printf 'last\n' > plain
rc=0; gzip hard shortcut plain || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && hard -ef peer && -L shortcut ]]
printf 'mixed-status=%s\n' "$rc"
gzip -d plain.gz
